messages:
Jordan (customer): Hey — hitting intermittent 403s in Safari when clicking "Generate". Happens ~1/4 attempts. Page shows "Request failed (403)" modal. No obvious UI repro beyond clicking the button. Using Safari 16.4 on macOS Ventura.

Ryan (support): Sorry about that Jordan — we can investigate. Can you grab a network HAR + console logs from Safari and attach them? Also please include the exact time (or a timestamp) when it happened so we can match server logs.

Jordan (customer): I can do that. Quick Q: how do I export HAR from Safari? I only know Chrome steps.

Ryan (support): Steps for Safari (short):
1) Enable Develop menu: Safari -> Settings -> Advanced -> check "Show Develop menu in menu bar".
2) Open the app and reproduce the 403. From the Develop menu choose "Show Web Inspector" (or press Option+Command+I).
3) In Web Inspector, go to the Network tab. Check "Preserve Log" (top-right).
4) Click the Generate button to reproduce.
5) Find the request to our frontend/backend (look for POST to /ui/generate or the API host). Right-click that request row -> "Export as HAR" (if available) or "Save as HAR".
6) In Console tab, right-click anywhere -> "Save as..." to capture console output (or copy visible errors).

If Safari doesn't show an "Export as HAR" option, two alternatives: a) open the page in Chrome/Edge and repeat the capture there (they have Export HAR), or b) use a local proxy like mitmproxy/Charles to save an HTTP archive. Either is fine.

Mira (eng): Also, please do the following before sending:
- In the Network tab select the failing request and look at Response Headers. Note the header `x-rd-request-id` (or `x-request-id`) value — paste that in the ticket. That's the single best way for us to find the server-side trace.
- In Console, look for an explicit message like "403 billing_required" or any stack trace. Screenshot that if possible.
- Redact your Authorization header / API key from the HAR (replace with "REDACTED"). We only need the request id and path.

Ryan (support): Curl repro (helps a lot) — replace <TOKEN> and <REQUEST_PAYLOAD> and run from Terminal (this will show headers):

```bash
curl -i -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

Look at the HTTP response headers for `x-rd-request-id` (or similar). If you get a 403 from curl too, paste the full response (headers + body) but please redact the token.

Jordan (customer): Got it. I checked Network -> Response Headers and I see "x-rd-request-id: 01H7A9XQ2Z9..." on one of the failed requests. I exported HAR (attached to the ticket) and saved Console as text. I also ran the curl and got a 403 with body: "{"error":"billing_required"}" — sent in the ticket.

Mira (eng): Thanks — that request id helps. A couple quick notes we might check while you wait:
- Is your org's billing card recently updated? 
- Are requests sometimes succeeding and sometimes failing? If so, we might be hitting a downstream auth cache or an intermittent third-party billing validation.
- Please include the exact user email / org id (in the support ticket) so we can correlate to billing records.

Jordan (customer): Card looks fine, billing portal says active. I attached HAR + console + curl output and included the x-rd-request-id. Also included the exact local time of the failure: 2026-03-17T15:22:41-07:00.

infra-bot: New support bundle received: attachments=har (safari-1842001111.har), console.txt, curl-output.txt; metadata: request_id=01H7A9XQ2Z9, user=jordan@example.com, user_agent=Safari/16.4 (Macintosh). Ticket ID #SUP-8921.

Ryan (support): Perfect — thanks Jordan. We'll triage. Eng (Mira) will pick this up and check backend traces for that request id. If we need a replay, we'll ask you to temporarily enable an org-level debug flag that increases logging.

Mira (eng): I pulled the server trace for 01H7A9XQ2Z9 — it shows a 403 from the billing validation service with message "billing_required" at 2026-03-17T22:22:41Z. I'll escalate to billing infra. In the meantime, can you try one experiment for us: log out of the app, open a private/incognito Safari window, sign in and try once more. That will rule out cookie/session edge cases.

Jordan (customer): Tried incognito — same 403. Anything else I can provide?

Mira (eng): No, that's perfect. We'll follow up in this thread with the billing team's findings. Thanks for the quick repro and for including the HAR + console + request id — that saved a lot of back-and-forth. :thumbsup:
